What it means: Mass of the incoming asteroid. For example, A1800 ≈ 10^18 kg and A2100 ≈ 10^21 kg. Its effect on BMF also depends on the other encounter conditions.
Closest distance between the asteroid and Mars. For example, r12 = 1.2 R_Mars (Mars-radii). Smaller values mean a closer encounter and stronger tidal forces.
Speed of the asteroid during the encounter. v00 is the lowest-speed case, while higher v codes represent faster encounters. Higher speeds generally make capture less likely.

Coverage range: none, x, y, z, mz; unevenly sampled
What it means: Rotation of the asteroid and the direction of its spin axis: none means no spin, x or y means equatorial spin, z means prograde z-spin, and mz means retrograde z-spin. Spin can change how the asteroid breaks up, but the different spin settings are unevenly sampled.
Number of SPH particles used in the simulation. For example, n65 is roughly 10^6.5 particles. This is a numerical setting rather than a physical property of the encounter.
Maximum distance used to decide whether nearby particles belong to the same fragment. It can change the measured fragments, but it does not change the physical encounter itself.
